name: Ipamorelin

b.x: Zero cortisol increase at 200 times the effective GH dose. That single data point from Raun et al. (1998) [1] explains why ipamorelin became the default starter peptide for growth hormone optimization. Ipamorelin (molecular weight ~711 Da) is a synthetic pentapeptide and selective GHS-R1a agonist. It binds the ghrelin receptor on pituitary somatotroph cells, producing a GH pulse within 15 to 30 minutes of subcutaneous injection. Gobburu and colleagues gave healthy men 15-minute IV infusions and modeled the result (1999) [2]. They measured a 2-hour half-life and one GH peak at about 40 minutes. The real-world use case is straightforward. Most users inject 100 to 300 mcg subcutaneously, one to three times daily on an empty stomach. Nearly everyone stacks it with CJC-1295 (no DAC), also called Mod GRF 1-29, to hit both GHS-R1a and GHRH receptor pathways simultaneously. That dual-pathway approach produces a GH pulse two to three times larger than either peptide alone. Bedtime dosing is the priority; the fasting window matters because insulin raises somatostatin, which fully blunts the GH response. Community evidence is strong. Hundreds of r/peptides threads (roughly 95,000 subscribers) consistently report improved sleep within one to two weeks, faster recovery by weeks three to four, and gradual body composition changes over six to twelve weeks. The scientific picture is less complete. The only published human RCT, a Phase 2 trial in 117 adults after bowel resection, missed its key endpoint versus placebo (Beck 2014) [6]. A second, 320-patient Phase 2 trial (NCT01280344) finished in 2014 without posted results or a paper. All efficacy data for anti-aging and body composition applications is community-derived. Preclinical work on bone mineral content (Svensson et al. 2000) [3] and cachexia (2024 ferret model) [4] looks promising but hasn't been replicated in humans.

Ipamorelin binds selectively to the growth hormone secretagogue receptor type 1a (GHS-R1a) on anterior pituitary somatotroph cells. This receptor is the same target ghrelin activates. Ipamorelin was developed for selective GH release, and users report far less hunger than on GHRP-6. In mice, ipamorelin raised body fat, and secretagogue treatment raised food intake (Lall et al. 2001) [8]. Once GHS-R1a activates, it triggers intracellular calcium signaling in somatotrophs, prompting GH vesicle release into circulation. In healthy men given 15-minute IV infusions, the GH pulse peaked at about 40 minutes (Gobburu et al. 1999) [2]. That pulse then stimulates hepatic IGF-1 production, the downstream mediator of most growth hormone effects on tissue repair, lipolysis, and protein synthesis. The selectivity is what sets ipamorelin apart. GHRP-2 and GHRP-6 both activate GHS-R1a but also stimulate ACTH release, cortisol secretion, and prolactin elevation at therapeutic doses. Raun et al. (1998) [1] demonstrated that ipamorelin produced no measurable cortisol or ACTH increase even at doses 200 times above the GH-effective threshold. This means it can be dosed multiple times daily without accumulating stress hormone burden. The 2-hour half-life [2] allows for a pulsatile dosing pattern that mimics natural GH secretion rhythms rather than creating the sustained tonic GH elevation seen with CJC-1295 (with DAC). Pairing ipamorelin with CJC-1295 (no DAC) hits both the GHS-R1a and GHRH receptor simultaneously, producing a complementary pulse roughly two to three times larger than either alone.
Ipamorelin benefits center on clean growth hormone optimization with the lowest side-effect burden of any GHRP available.
No cortisol or prolactin elevation in swine. Raun et al. found no prolactin rise, and no ACTH or cortisol rise even at more than 200 times the GH-releasing dose [1].
Improved deep sleep quality within one to two weeks of starting, the most consistently first-reported benefit across hundreds of r/peptides threads.
Exposure rose in step with dose across five IV infusion levels in healthy men, and the half-life held at 2 hours [2].
Less hunger than GHRP-6, by user reports, which suits fat-loss goals. No human study has measured hunger on it. In mice, it raised body fat (Lall et al. 2001) [8].

Bone mineral content improvements documented in rodent models at 12-plus weeks of dosing (Svensson et al. 2000; Andersen et al. 2001) [3] [5], with the compound also countering glucocorticoid-induced bone loss.
No receptor desensitization documented with continuous use, unlike hexarelin. The 12-on/4-off cycling protocol is precautionary rather than evidence-based for ipamorelin specifically.
Partially Aligned
Scientific Evidence
Based on 9 key studies · Research only
Mechanism well-established: selective GHS-R1a agonist producing a clean GH pulse without cortisol, ACTH, or prolactin co-activation in swine (Raun et al. 1998) [1].
Dosing studied: 100–300 mcg per injection (community-derived); 1–3 injections per day (no clinical trial established an optimal frequency)

Human PK-PD used 15-minute IV infusions in healthy men (Gobburu et al. 1999) [2]. It found a ~2h half-life, dose-proportional kinetics and one GH peak at ~40 min. The only published human RCT (Phase 2, postoperative ileus after bowel resection, n=117; Beck 2014) [6] showed no efficacy vs. placebo; a second Phase 2 trial (NCT01280344, n=320, completed 2014) never posted results. Ipamorelin has never passed a positive human efficacy trial. No new human RCTs published 2024–2026; new 2024 animal data [4] supports cachexia application but is preclinical only.
Key Study

Raun et al. 1998 (PMID 9849822): established ipamorelin as first selective GHS; no cortisol/ACTH elevation even at 200× the effective GH dose. Gobburu et al. 1999 (PMID 10496658): human PK-PD modeling after 15-minute IV infusions in healthy men; 2h half-life, dose-proportional PK, GH peak at ~40 min.
Limitations

Only published human RCT (Phase 2, postoperative ileus after bowel resection, PMID 25331030) missed its key endpoint; a second Phase 2 trial (NCT01280344) never posted results. No approved clinical indication. All long-term dosing and efficacy data is community-derived. Preclinical findings (bone, fat) not replicated in a human trial. New 2024 cachexia study (PMID 39043357) is ferret model only.
Community Experience
Widely regarded as the safest and most beginner-friendly GHRP.
Community dosing: 100–300 mcg per injection, 1–3× daily; most common: 200 mcg ipamorelin + 100 mcg CJC-1295 (no DAC), 1–2× daily

"Cleanest GHRP": no cortisol, prolactin, or appetite spike vs. GHRP-2 and GHRP-6. Almost universally stacked with CJC-1295 (no DAC) rather than used solo. Primary uses: GH optimization, sleep quality, body recomposition, recovery.

Science and community agree on GHS-R1a mechanism, selectivity vs. other GHRPs, GH pulse characteristics, and 2h half-life. Community dosing of 100–300 mcg/injection aligns with published PK-PD dose-response data. Key divergence: the only published human RCT (postoperative ileus, Phase 2) failed vs. placebo, while community consistently reports sleep and body composition benefits from off-label use. Community applications differ from the failed clinical indication. Fasting window requirement is mechanistically sound (insulin→somatostatin→blunted GH pulse).

With a 2 mg vial and 2 mL bacteriostatic water, you'll get 1,000 mcg/mL. Each 100 mcg dose is 10 units on an insulin syringe. A 5 mg vial reconstituted with 2 mL gives 2,500 mcg/mL, so 200 mcg is 8 units and 300 mcg is 12 units per injection. The fasting window is the thing most beginners mess up. You need at least two hours with no food before injection. Insulin triggers somatostatin release, which completely blocks the GH pulse. Eating within that window isn't "suboptimal"; it negates the injection entirely. No food for 30 minutes after, either. Bedtime dosing is priority number one. It amplifies the natural nocturnal GH pulse. If you're dosing twice daily, the morning shot should be fasted on waking. Space injections at least eight hours apart. Store lyophilized vials at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius. After reconstitution, keep refrigerated and use within three to four weeks. Toss anything cloudy or with particles floating in it. If you see zero sleep improvement after two weeks with correct fasting timing, suspect the product before blaming the protocol. Get an IGF-1 lab at week four to confirm the peptide is actually working. Product quality varies significantly.
Cycling Protocol
Cycle to maintain receptor sensitivity. Can also be run 5 days on, 2 off weekly.
Ipamorelin Cycle

Ipamorelin has notably lower desensitization risk than other GHRPs (especially hexarelin) due to GHS-R1a selectivity and absence of ACTH pathway activation. The 12-week on/4-week off cycle is precautionary, not evidence-based specifically for ipamorelin. No published RCT-level data on ipamorelin-specific desensitization or tachyphylaxis in humans. Community experience and analog literature support cycling to maintain pituitary somatotroph sensitivity and natural GH axis rhythm. Some longevity clinics run 5 days on/2 days off weekly cycling as an alternative within longer-duration protocols. Extended continuous use (>16 weeks) has produced community-reported diminishing returns, particularly in sleep improvement.

No human study has measured intranasal or subcutaneous bioavailability. In male rats, intranasal bioavailability was about 20% (PMID 9879640). No dose conversion is established.
Not used in practice due to low and variable mucosal absorption. No standardized intranasal protocol exists in community or clinical settings. SC injection remains the only practical route.

Avoid
GHRP-6

Concurrent use of two GHRPs causes receptor competition at GHS-R1a with no additional GH benefit. GHRP-6's intense hunger and ghrelin-pathway activation defeats the primary reason to choose ipamorelin (less hunger than GHRP-6, by user reports). Stack one GHRP only.
GHRP-2

Competing GHRPs at the same GHS-R1a receptor: no additive GH benefit documented. GHRP-2 adds cortisol and prolactin co-elevation that ipamorelin specifically avoids. Defeats the rationale for choosing ipamorelin. Choose one GHRP per stack.
CJC-1295 (with DAC)

DAC version's days-long half-life creates sustained tonic GH stimulation that mismatches ipamorelin's pulsatile mechanism. Suppresses natural nocturnal GH peaks and pituitary pulsatility over time. Use CJC-1295 no-DAC (Mod GRF 1-29) instead.
Exogenous HGH (recombinant GH / somatropin)

Combining GH secretagogues with exogenous HGH saturates the GH axis, suppresses endogenous pulsatility, and eliminates the primary rationale for secretagogue use (axis preservation). Dramatically increases IGF-1 overshoot and side-effect risk.

The most serious risk with ipamorelin is IGF-1 overshoot. Sustained supraphysiological IGF-1 levels carry a theoretical cancer promotion risk, particularly in anyone with active malignancy or a history of cancer. GH promotes cell proliferation. That's the mechanism behind its benefits and its biggest concern. If IGF-1 climbs above the age-adjusted upper normal range on two consecutive readings, the protocol should stop. Carpal tunnel symptoms (tingling or numbness in the hands) are the clearest signal that GH levels have gone too high. Community reports flag this primarily at the aggressive tier (300 mcg three times daily). This isn't a "push through it" side effect. Tingling means stop immediately, wait at least four weeks, and restart at a lower dose and frequency if appropriate. Water retention is common, especially at twice-daily or three-times-daily dosing. Mild puffiness around the face or ankles is the typical presentation. Reducing injection frequency (not dose) is the first adjustment. Transient headache within 30 to 60 minutes of injection is expected and relates directly to the acute GH pulse. It resolves within hours for most users. Cutting the dose by 25% usually handles persistent headache. Injection-site reactions (mild redness, irritation) are reported frequently in the first two weeks and tend to resolve with consistent site rotation. Abdomen is the preferred injection location. Occasional lightheadedness immediately post-injection is reported but typically mild. Published side effect data in humans is limited. Only one human RCT has been published (Phase 2, 117 adults after bowel resection) [6]. It used intravenous dosing and tracked adverse events, but its endpoints were GI recovery, not the subcutaneous anti-aging use case. A second Phase 2 trial in 320 bowel-resection patients (NCT01280344) finished in 2014 and never posted results. Community side-effect reporting across hundreds of threads is remarkably consistent, which provides reasonable confidence in the profile above, but formal incidence rates don't exist for the off-label application. GH release antagonizes insulin action. Fasting glucose should be monitored at baseline, week six, and week twelve. Anyone with uncontrolled diabetes or severe insulin resistance should not use ipamorelin. A fasting glucose above 126 mg/dL means discontinuation. Pregnancy and breastfeeding are contraindicated due to insufficient safety data. GH supplementation can also unmask subclinical hypothyroidism by accelerating T4-to-T3 conversion; thyroid monitoring (TSH, fT3) is recommended at baseline. When to see a doctor: persistent hand tingling or numbness, significant edema, fasting glucose above 126 mg/dL, any visual changes, or symptoms of intracranial hypertension.
Common Issues & Solutions

No IGF-1 change after 6–8 weeks: most common cause is eating within 2 hours before injection: insulin raises somatostatin and fully blunts the GH pulse. Verify fasting compliance before blaming product quality. Then a batch-specific CoA can rule out underdosing or degradation.
Transient headache within 30–60 min of injection: expected with acute GH release; resolves within hours. Reduce dose by 25% if severe or lasting. Ensure adequate hydration pre-injection.

Water retention or hand tingling: reduce injection frequency first (not dose). Tingling/numbness in hands = early carpal tunnel sign: stop immediately and allow 4+ weeks recovery before restarting at lower dose.

Results much slower than expected: ipamorelin is not an acute performance compound: visible body composition changes require 6–12 weeks minimum. Common error is comparing onset timeline to anabolic steroids. IGF-1 lab confirmation at week 4–6 can confirm the protocol is working before visible changes appear.

Suspected product quality issue: CJC-1295 DAC/no-DAC mislabeling is common in lower-quality products. If stacking and seeing no sleep improvement in week 1–2 despite correct timing, suspect product substitution. A CoA specifying ipamorelin molecular weight (~711 Da) is the only way to confirm identity.

Ipamorelin: Product Quality medium risk

No GMP requirement applies to "research use only" products. Ipamorelin (MW ~711 Da) is a smaller, simpler peptide than CJC-1295 (~3.4 kDa), making synthesis somewhat more consistent, but quality variance across brands remains significant. Key risks: (1) underdosing: peptide content lower than labeled, reducing efficacy; (2) DAC/no-DAC mislabeling is less of an issue for pure ipamorelin than for CJC blends, but still documented; (3) degradation from improper storage or reconstitution. Independent product testing (Finnrick Analytics) shows purity ranges from ~70% to 99.95% across GHRP brands. Athletes: ipamorelin is on WADA 2026 Prohibited List (S2.2.4: GH Releasing Factors); contamination risk from non-dedicated facilities.

Ipamorelin is classified as "research use only" in the United States. It has no FDA approval for any clinical indication. Two Phase 2 trials for GI recovery after bowel resection were completed (NCT00672074 and NCT01280344), and neither led to an approved application. FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee voted against adding ipamorelin to the 503A bulks list on October 29, 2024. Both forms (acetate and free base) drew 0 yes, 12 no and 1 abstention. The vote is advisory, and FDA has not ruled on the listing. Ipamorelin is not on the 503A bulks list (21 CFR 216.23). FDA's Category 2 page (current as of April 22, 2026) still lists ipamorelin acetate for 503B outsourcing facilities, added September 29, 2023. FDA cites immunogenicity risk and a published intravenous gastric-motility study that reported serious adverse events, including death. Some telehealth and anti-aging clinics prescribe ipamorelin, typically in a combination with CJC-1295. Athletes: ipamorelin is on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List under S2.2.4 (Growth Hormone Releasing Factors). It is detectable via urine immunoassay. Any athlete subject to anti-doping testing should not use this compound. This content is for educational and research purposes only. Nothing here constitutes medical advice. Consult a licensed healthcare provider before using any peptide.

faqs.q: Should I stack with CJC-1295 with DAC or without DAC?
faqs.a: Without DAC, also called Mod GRF 1-29. The DAC version creates a sustained GH "bleed" instead of a pulse, which doesn't match ipamorelin's pulsatile mechanism and can blunt your natural GH rhythm over time. The no-DAC version has an estimated ~30-minute half-life and should be injected simultaneously with ipamorelin 2-3x daily. Some clinics sell pre-mixed blends.

faqs.q: How long until I notice results?
faqs.a: Sleep quality usually improves first, often within 1-2 weeks. Recovery improvements show up at weeks 3-4. Visible body composition changes (fat loss, muscle fullness) take 6-8 weeks minimum of consistent use. IGF-1 lab changes are measurable at 4 weeks. This is a slow-burn compound, not an acute performance drug.

faqs.q: Can ipamorelin be run indefinitely without desensitization?
faqs.a: Unlike hexarelin, ipamorelin doesn't cause receptor desensitization with continuous use. The standard 12-on/4-off cycle is precautionary, not evidence-based for ipamorelin specifically. A 2-year study showed no pituitary suppression with a related GHS. Some longevity clinics run it continuously with monitoring.

faqs.q: Why doesn't ipamorelin spike appetite like GHRP-6?
faqs.a: Both bind the same ghrelin receptor (GHS-R1a), so the difference rests mostly on user reports. Community reports describe strong hunger about 20 minutes after GHRP-6 and little or none on ipamorelin. Raun et al. 1998 (PMID 9849822) is often credited with this, but that swine study did not measure appetite. It measured hormones: ipamorelin raised GH without raising ACTH or cortisol, while GHRP-6 and GHRP-2 raised both.

faqs.q: What's the difference between ipamorelin and sermorelin?
faqs.a: Different receptor pathways entirely. Sermorelin is a GHRH analog (acts on GHRH receptors); ipamorelin is a GHRP (acts on GHS-R1a). Sermorelin produces a more physiological GH pulse. Community reports call ipamorelin's pulse faster and stronger per dose; no human study has tested that ranking. For best results, stack both or combine ipamorelin with Mod GRF 1-29 to hit both pathways. If picking just one, community reports favor ipamorelin.

faqs.q: What is the recommended Ipamorelin dosage?
faqs.a: Ipamorelin dosing varies by experience level. Beginners typically start at 100 mcg daily, moderate users at 200 mcg 2x daily, and aggressive protocols use 300 mcg 3x daily.
Ipamorelin typically comes in 2mg or 5mg vials. Add 2mL of bacteriostatic water to the vial. Use the free calculator for exact syringe units based on your desired dose.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of Ipamorelin?
faqs.a: The half-life of Ipamorelin is ~2 hours. This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.

summary: , and users report little hunger. No human efficacy trial has succeeded yet; the only published Phase 2 RCT missed its endpoint, and a second never posted results. Still, hundreds of r/peptides threads and a 4.5/5 community sentiment score put ipamorelin in the top five most-discussed peptides. Adults looking for GH optimization with the fewest hormonal side effects start here, usually stacked with CJC-1295 (no DAC).
